observations: Photo 0 shows a Toyota V6-style engine bay assembly on the ground with many hoses/wiring harnesses attached; visible intake/throttle area and multiple coolant/AC-related lines.
Photo 1 shows the same engine assembly from another angle; a large black intake/airbox component is visible along with more wiring and pipework.
Photo 2 shows the engine with the upper cover/airbox area and a large silver/metal component; the transmission/gearbox section appears attached or included (large casing at the bottom).
No clear engine code, VIN, or model number is readable in any photo.

The seller’s text claims it is a complete engine with compressor and operators for Toyota Venza/Camry/Sienna/Highlander, but the photos do not clearly confirm the exact vehicle fitment or that a compressor is included.

claims.claim: Complete engine with compressor and all the operators for Toyota Venza, Camry, Sienna, Highlander,...
claims.evidence: Photos show an engine assembly with hoses/wiring and what looks like attached components, but no readable part labels/codes and no clear, confirmable compressor/“operators” identification.

risks.risk: Wrong engine variant/fitment (different Toyota Venza/Camry/Sienna/Highlander engines and years use different engine codes, wiring, and mounts).
risks.proof: Ask for a clear photo of the engine code/label (usually on the engine block or cylinder head) and the transmission code/label, plus the donor car year/model.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst-case: not confirmed correct fitment for the buyer’s exact Toyota and may require extra parts/wiring/ECU changes.

risks.risk: “Compressor” may be missing or not the correct AC compressor for the engine/AC system.
risks.proof: Ask for a close-up photo of the AC compressor body with its label/part number, and a photo showing it physically mounted to the assembly.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst-case: compressor not included or not usable for AC.

risks.risk: Engine may be incomplete (missing sensors, brackets, alternator/AC lines, starter, ECU, or key harness connectors).
risks.proof: Ask for a full inventory photo laid out (ECU, alternator, starter, sensors, belts, AC lines, relays/fuses) and a photo of every connector end.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst-case: incomplete and may need replacement of missing parts.

risks.risk: Unknown mechanical condition (compression, internal wear, oil leaks, timing/chain condition). Photos cannot confirm running condition.
risks.proof: Ask for a short video of the engine running (cold start if possible) or at least a compression test sheet from the workshop.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst-case: not proven working.

risks.risk: Transmission/gearbox condition and compatibility (photo suggests gearbox is included, but condition and type are not confirmed).
risks.proof: Ask for a photo of the transmission model/label and a video showing gear engagement (or a test report).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst-case: gearbox condition not proven.

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the engine code/label (engine block/cylinder head) and transmission code/label.
Close-up photo showing the AC compressor clearly (with label/part number) and confirmation it is included and mounted.
Video of the engine starting/running (or compression test report).
Inventory photos: ECU, alternator, starter, major sensors, and all connectors/harness ends; show any missing items if not included.
response.reason: The photos show a Toyota engine/gearbox assembly, but the exact engine variant and whether the AC compressor and required “operators” are truly included and compatible cannot be confirmed remotely. Without engine/transmission codes and proof of working condition, a reliable worst-case price cannot be set.
